title: Machine-readable per-building transcription of validation/visual_audit.json
disclaimer: Faithful mechanical transcription of the assessments in validation/visual_audit.json: model-assisted readings of single-epoch 15 cm RGB orthophoto imagery. These annotations are NOT labelled ground truth, NOT an accuracy measurement and NOT human validation; independent human review would be required before operational use. No assessment was invented, upgraded or softened in transcription (the mapping applied is recorded under assessment_mapping), every note is carried verbatim, and no published value, geometry or confidence may be changed on the basis of this file - the pipeline attaches it as report blocks and review flags only.

audit_basis.note: The audit examined the EARLIER baseline artifact identified by audited_document_sha256 at baseline_commit - not the artifact of any run this file is attached to, whose bytes differ by design (the pipeline has been corrected since). A future human re-audit of a final artifact would record that artifact's sha256 in reaudit_of_artifact_sha256; until then release tooling must report the audit binding as baseline-only.

status_vocabulary.supports: the audit's reading is consistent with the published output
status_vocabulary.questionable: the audit doubts this aspect; a human should look
status_vocabulary.conflicts: the audit's reading disagrees with the published output; the published value stands unchanged
status_vocabulary.not_judgeable: the audit could not judge this aspect from the imagery

summary_policy: Each annotation additionally carries code (aspect.status, a stable machine key) and summary (a concise <=140-character distillation of the verbatim note, written for embedding in the output document). The summary is a faithful condensation, never an upgraded or softened assessment; the note in this file remains the verbatim evidence trail and the authority.

vie-swv-001.note: Ring follows the outer roof edge on all four sides; the 238.9 m2 courtyard void is correctly cut out. Any outward bias is <=0.5 m and not separable from a parapet/eave at this GSD.

vie-swv-001.note: Single-level deck with parapet, plant boxes and module rows; no ridge, no two differently-facing planes.

vie-swv-001.note: No ridge discernible; abstention well founded.

vie-swv-001.note: Most of the visible surface is covered BY MODULES, so the classifier largely describes the panel field and the reddish perimeter band.

vie-swv-001.note: No occlusion, no missing tiles, roof interior fully lit.

vie-swv-002.note: Multiple wings, all flat decks with raised light-coloured wing roofs; no ridge anywhere.

vie-swv-002.note: 149 lines but dominant orientation carries only 10% of line length - expected on a many-wing flat complex.

vie-swv-002.note: Published 'mixed'; the 'tiled' component is a defensible colour match on warm reddish-brown pixels, but this is a modern flat roof and those same pixels are the dormant-substrate signature.

vie-swv-002.summary: No occlusion and no missing data; roof interiors lit.
vie-swv-002.note: No occlusion or missing data; roof interiors lit.

vie-swv-003.summary: Simple rectangle following the roof edge on all four sides; the gravel border strip is roof, not ground.
vie-swv-003.note: Simple rectangle following the roof edge on all four sides; reddish-brown gravel border strip is roof, not ground.

vie-swv-003.summary: Auth->CV median 0.44 m, max 1.32 m; highest boundary_gradient_ratio in the set (1.805). Evidence only.
vie-swv-003.note: Auth->CV median 0.44 m, max 1.32 m. Highest boundary_gradient_ratio in A's set (1.805): the CV boundary sits on markedly stronger image structure. Evidence only.

vie-swv-003.summary: Reads as one plane with flush module fields; at SLOPE_MEAN 7.94 deg a shallow monopitch and flat-with-fall are not separable.
vie-swv-003.note: Reads as one plane with two flush module fields and a central plant spine; no ridge. But at SLOPE_MEAN 7.94 deg a shallow monopitch and a flat roof with fall are not separable at 10 cm/px. SOFT disagreement, not a conflict.

vie-swv-003.summary: Strongest line is within 0.6 deg of the footprint axis - almost certainly the parapet; the contrast gate correctly refused it.
vie-swv-003.note: Strongest line 159.34 deg is within 0.6 deg of footprint axis 158.73 deg - almost certainly the long parapet; plane-contrast gate (12.8% vs 15%) correctly refused it.

vie-swv-003.summary: Low information: most of the visible roof is modules.
vie-swv-003.note: Low information: the majority of the visible roof is modules.

vie-swv-003.summary: Roof interior fully lit; the large dark area to the east is ground shadow outside the polygon.
vie-swv-003.note: Roof interior fully lit; the large dark area east is ground shadow outside the polygon.

vie-swv-004.summary: Tracks the curved edge well but has NO interior hole; the enclosed inner area reads as a lower deck. Imagery cannot settle it.
vie-swv-004.note: Line tracks the curved edge well (243 vertices). The issue is that this polygon has NO interior hole while 001 and 002 have theirs cut out; the enclosed inner area reads as a lower landscaped/terrace deck. Evidence favours a built-over podium (FMZK IoU 0.985, symmetric containment 0.992) but imagery cannot settle it.

vie-swv-004.summary: Tightest in the set (median 0.27 m, max 1.00 m); CV reproduces the no-hole topology, adding no evidence on the courtyard question.
vie-swv-004.note: Tightest in A's set: median 0.27 m, max 1.00 m. CV reproduces the no-hole topology, so it adds no independent evidence on the courtyard question.

vie-swv-004.summary: Two large surfaces read flat; the light band on the curved perimeter could be sloping roof or sunlit parapet. SLOPE_MEAN 7.82 deg.
vie-swv-004.note: Two large visible surfaces read flat; the light band following the curved perimeter could be a sloping perimeter roof or a sunlit parapet. SLOPE_MEAN 7.82 deg.

vie-swv-004.summary: A curved organic roof has no single ridge; the dominant orientation carries only 9% of line length.
vie-swv-004.note: A curved organic roof has no single ridge; dominant orientation carries only 9% of line length.

vie-swv-004.summary: Neutral light grey, fine texture; a light membrane or paved deck would look similar; 'unclear' equally acceptable.
vie-swv-004.note: Neutral light grey, fine texture. A light membrane or paved deck would look similar; 'unclear' equally acceptable.

vie-swv-004.summary: Fully lit, no missing tiles; bare-crown street trees do not reach the roof.
vie-swv-004.note: Fully lit, no missing tiles, bare-crown street trees do not reach the roof.

vie-swv-005.summary: Follows the roof edge north, west and east; the south-east striped strip the CV excludes is not judgeable on that edge.
vie-swv-005.note: Follows the roof edge north, west and east. The south/south-east edge includes a lighter finely striped strip that the CV excludes - canopy, awning or bright membrane; that specific edge is not_judgeable.

vie-swv-005.summary: Lowest agreement in the set: the CV drops the southern strip, 503 vs 547 m2 (~8% smaller). Systematic, not noise.
vie-swv-005.note: Lowest agreement in A's set. The CV drops the southern strip, cutting a straight diagonal across the authoritative step. CV 503 m2 vs auth 547 m2 (~8% smaller). Systematic, not noise.

vie-swv-005.summary: Uniform single-level pale grey deck with parapet and small units along the eastern edge.
vie-swv-005.note: Uniform single-level pale grey deck with parapet and a row of small units along the eastern edge.

vie-swv-005.summary: Only 5 co-oriented lines - the rectangular parapet; plane-contrast could not run on a roof this small.
vie-swv-005.note: Only 5 lines, all co-oriented (dominant share 1.0) - the rectangular parapet. Plane-contrast could not be run on a roof this small.

vie-swv-005.summary: Weakest majority in the set (57%); light membrane and light gravel ballast are not separable here; 'unclear' acceptable.
vie-swv-005.note: Weakest majority in A's set (57%). A light single-ply membrane and light gravel ballast are not separable here; 'unclear' acceptable.

vie-swv-005.summary: Best-lit in the set; adjacent structures shadow the street but not the roof interior.
vie-swv-005.note: Best-lit in A's set; adjacent structures shadow the street but not the roof interior.

vie-swv-006.summary: Tracks the parapet band cleanly; open question: zero interior rings yet 3-4 dark voids (~10-12% of area) unclear at this GSD.
vie-swv-006.note: Tracks the parapet band cleanly on all four sides. OPEN QUESTION: the outline has zero interior rings yet the roof contains 3-4 dark rectangular voids (~20, ~27, ~20 m2, of order 10-12% of 597.9 m2). Open light wells or dark-glazed rooflights - unclear at this GSD.

vie-swv-006.summary: CV bulges ~1-1.5 m outward on the west and NE corner and cuts the north notch; 611.5 vs 597.9 m2.
vie-swv-006.note: Magenta bulges ~1-1.5 m outward on the west and at the NE corner and cuts the north notch. CV 611.5 m2 vs auth 597.9 m2.

vie-swv-006.summary: Large single deck with parapets and plant/rooflight strips; no second plane.
vie-swv-006.note: Large single deck with parapets, plant and rooflight strips; no second plane.

vie-swv-006.summary: No ridge visible; dominant orientation came from the plant/rooflight spine and the contrast gate correctly refused it.
vie-swv-006.note: No ridge visible. Dominant orientation was driven by the long grey plant/rooflight spine; the 15% contrast gate (8.5% measured) correctly refused it.

vie-swv-006.summary: Published bitumen_gravel (85%) but the dominant warm-toned mat could be reddish ballast or dormant sedum - not separable here.
vie-swv-006.note: Published bitumen_gravel (85%). The dominant surface is a fine mottled WARM-toned mat in bays separated by pale paver walkways: R-B +14 to +22 vs grey plant at -13 to -16. Reddish ballast and dormant sedum are not separable here.

vie-swv-006.summary: No interior shadow, no occlusion, no missing tiles; fully judgeable.
vie-swv-006.note: No shadow over the interior, no occlusion, no missing tiles, fully judgeable.

vie-swv-007.summary: Both wings tracked well; two ~1 m2 interior rings are real light shafts. Partial shadow from a taller neighbour on the east flank.
vie-swv-007.note: Both wings tracked well; follows the eaves/gutter line of the street wing and the stepped rear elevation. Two ~1 m2 interior rings are real light shafts visible beside chimney stacks. Partial shadow from a taller neighbour on the east flank.

vie-swv-007.summary: Exterior agreement good; the divergence is topological - the CV is a simple polygon while the authoritative geometry has two rings.
vie-swv-007.note: Exterior-ring agreement is good (max 1.48 m auth->cv, 1.043 m cv->auth (remeasured in Phase 4A)). The divergence is TOPOLOGICAL: the CV output is a simple Polygon with no holes while the authoritative geometry carries two interior rings.

vie-swv-007.summary: The roof-type reading is unambiguous on both wings.
Could not falsify: a bright continuous ridge line with a self-shadowed and a lit plane; near-square footprint makes the axis arbitrary.
vie-swv-007.note: B looked hard and could not falsify it. A bright continuous ridge line runs lower-left to upper-right on the NW wing with a dark self-shadowed NW-facing plane above and a lit pinkish-tan tiled plane below. The perpendicular-to-long-axis concern carries no weight here: the min-rotated-rectangle is 31.66 x 27.43 m, elongation 1.154 - near-square, so the long axis is essentially arbitrary.

vie-swv-007.summary: Published 'mixed'; reads mostly tile with a large self-shadowed plane likely binned into other classes - not three real materials.
vie-swv-007.note: Published 'mixed'. B reads predominantly clay/concrete tile on both lit planes with a very large self-shadowed NW plane; the shadowed tiled plane is likely being binned into bitumen_gravel/metal. 'mixed' is defensible as a label; the shares are not three real materials.

vie-swv-007.summary: The NW plane is in deep self-shadow (~a third of the outline) and the east flank shadowed, yet shadow_fraction publishes 0.0.
vie-swv-007.note: Good over the lit planes, but the NW-facing plane is in deep self-shadow across roughly a third of the outline and the east flank is shadowed by a taller neighbour - while the record publishes shadow_fraction 0.0 / judgeable_fraction 1.0.

vie-swv-008.summary: The ~38 m south-east side encloses what reads as a building facade (windowed band seen obliquely); NW corner over open shadow.
vie-swv-008.note: The entire ~38 m south-east long side of the outline encloses what reads as a BUILDING FACADE, not a roof: a 5-8 m wide mid-grey band containing regularly spaced window openings with visible glazing bars, frames and reveals, seen obliquely. The NW corner sits over open shadow.

vie-swv-008.summary: CV 641.0 vs 682.4 m2 (-6%): consistently trims the shadowed NW wedge and the SW strip; no warning fired (Hausdorff 1.69 m).
vie-swv-008.note: CV 641.0 m2 vs auth 682.4 m2 (-6%). Magenta consistently trims the shadowed NW/N wedge and the SW pavement-side strip. Understandable as GrabCut excluding low-luminance regions; no warning fired (Hausdorff 1.69 m).

vie-swv-008.summary: Visual reading is flat (bright deck, skylights, penthouse, plant); no pitched plane pair. The authoritative value is NOT overridden.
vie-swv-008.note: B's VISUAL reading is flat: a large bright near-uniform deck, skylight strips or roof monitors, a raised penthouse and substantial mechanical plant. No pair of differently-facing pitched planes covers this footprint. The authoritative value is NOT overridden and B recommends no change.

vie-swv-008.summary: The detected 65.24 deg edge is the bright deck / dark facade boundary, not a ridge; erosion cannot keep the 5-8 m band out.
vie-swv-008.note: The detected 65.24 deg is within 0.24 deg of footprint_axis_orientation_deg 65.00. The strongest ~65 deg brightness edge is the boundary between the bright deck (mean lum ~201) and the dark facade band (~151-116) - a deck/parapet/facade boundary, not a ridge between two roof planes. Interior erosion is 1.5 m and contrast is sampled +/-1.5 m, nowhere near enough to keep a 5-8 m wide band out of the search.

vie-swv-008.summary: Plausible for the visible deck, but ~20% 'metal' and the facade band are classified as roof surface when they read as a wall.
vie-swv-008.note: Plausible for the visible deck (light-grey membrane/ballast), but ~20% 'metal' and the whole facade band are being classified as roof surface when they are, on B's reading, a wall.

vie-swv-008.summary: Deck fully readable but the NW third of the outline is open shadow, yet shadow_fraction publishes 0.0.
vie-swv-008.note: The deck is bright and fully readable; the NW third of the outline is open shadow (mean ~116, p05 ~73 on the overlay) yet shadow_fraction publishes 0.0.

vie-swv-009.summary: A dumbbell over a courtyard or low link; the eastern block's outline extends further east than the CV, over a dark strip.
vie-swv-009.note: A dumbbell: two roof blocks joined by a narrow neck over what appears to be a courtyard or low link. The western block is well tracked; on the eastern block the outline extends noticeably further east than the CV, over a strip that is dark in the imagery.

vie-swv-009.summary: Max separation 2.44 m at the eastern edge and the neck, which the CV smooths into an arc; 463.5 vs 454.9 m2.
vie-swv-009.note: Max separation 2.44 m at the eastern edge and around the neck; the CV smooths the neck's stepped geometry into an arc. CV 463.5 m2 vs auth 454.9 m2.

vie-swv-009.summary: Articulated surface, but shallow multi-plane geometry and flat-with-raised-strips are not separable at 10 cm/px.
vie-swv-009.note: The surface is articulated with what could be valleys and hips, but at 10 cm/px shallow multi-plane geometry and a flat roof with raised strips are not separable. The immediate neighbour to the north IS an unmistakable red-tiled pitched roof, and 009 does not look like it.

vie-swv-009.summary: Only 1 of 2 segments agreed, so no ridge was published; the abstention is honest and not evidence of a flat roof.
vie-swv-009.note: Only 1 of 2 segments agreed, so no ridge was published. B cannot assert a ridge either. The abstention is honest and is not evidence of a flat roof.

vie-swv-009.summary: Light beige/grey granular with darker seams; on an 1891, 38.9 deg record tile might be expected - tiled share is 0.08%.
vie-swv-009.note: Light beige/grey granular with darker seams. Worth flagging only that on a BAUJAHR 1891, 38.9 deg record one might have expected tile; tiled share is 0.08%.

vie-swv-009.summary: Lit roof surfaces readable; the eastern and southern margins and the neck sit in shadow; no missing tiles.
vie-swv-009.note: Lit roof surfaces readable; eastern and southern margins and the neck sit in shadow. No missing tiles.

vie-swv-010.summary: Southern ~55% is a legible flat deck; whether the dark northern ~45% is roof at all is not judgeable; tree over the NW corner.
vie-swv-010.note: Roughly the southern 55% is a bright legible flat deck; the northern ~45% is a large dark region (shadowed rear courtyard or dark rear roof) that B cannot resolve, with a bare tree crown overhanging the NW corner. Whether the north half is roof at all is not judgeable.

vie-swv-010.summary: Best agreement in absolute terms (383.7 vs 385.0 m2, gradient ratio near parity); separation <=1.5 m everywhere.
vie-swv-010.note: Best agreement in B's set in absolute terms (383.7 vs 385.0 m2; boundary_gradient_ratio 1.0165, closest to parity). Separation <=1.5 m everywhere.

vie-swv-010.summary: Readable southern half reads flat, northern half unreadable; SLOPE_MEAN 12.00 deg sits in the 10-15 deg abstain band.
vie-swv-010.note: The readable southern half reads flat; the northern half is unreadable. SLOPE_MEAN 12.00 deg sits inside the 10-15 deg fallback abstain band.

vie-swv-010.summary: The lit-deck/dark-region step could satisfy the contrast gate; only 3 segments, and ~74 deg off a meaningfully defined axis is odd.
vie-swv-010.note: The lit deck (~180) against the dark northern region (~91) is a ~2:1 step, comfortably enough for the reported 28.6% plane contrast, and the boundary runs at roughly the reported orientation. Only 3 Hough segments, longest 10.0 m - the minimum viable configuration. Footprint axis 170.33 deg vs ridge 64.74 deg is ~74 deg apart, and here the axis IS meaningfully defined (elongation 1.672), so the perpendicularity is a genuine oddity.

vie-swv-010.summary: 55% is a bare majority and a large share of the outline is the unreadable dark region; 'mixed' at least as defensible.
vie-swv-010.note: 55% is a bare majority and a large share of the outline is the unreadable dark region; 'mixed' would have been at least as defensible.

vie-swv-010.summary: Poorest in the set: ~45% of the outline is dark and unreadable, a tree over the NW corner, yet shadow_fraction publishes 0.0.
vie-swv-010.note: Poorest in B's set: ~45% of the outline is a dark, effectively unreadable region and a bare tree crown overhangs the NW corner - yet shadow_fraction publishes 0.0 and judgeable_fraction 1.0.
